keys.description: W2-03 (LIB-13; W-06, W-09, I-8). `true`: raw storage keeps every role, and derivation reads only what the role allows. A system or tool turn is written (not skipped by `firewall.skip_message_roles`) and tagged `derive_use:excluded` / `derive_use:evidence`; user and operator turns are `stated`, assistant turns `proposal`. Window extraction (`write.window_extract`) and the session-close and session-stage inputs drop system turns and echoes (`turns_excluded_excluded` / `turns_excluded_echo` in the window counters); a fact backed only by assistant or tool turns is tagged `derive_use:proposal` / `evidence`. The raw record's provenance class comes from the role (assistant `assistant_proposed`, tool `tool`) and its trust is capped at the user-stated level, never raised. Echo guard: a non-user turn that carries a recall marker (the engine's own context wrappers or `wrap_recall`) or overlaps a memory the session's last read returned (max of Jaccard and containment of 3-token shingles, at least `write.echo_threshold`) is tagged `echo` and `echo_of:<id>` and is never re-derived as a new fact; a user turn that restates a shown memory is tagged `assent_candidate` and never counts as support. Needs a `session_id` on both the read and the write for the overlap check. A turn that carries `entity` + `attribute` (optionally `value`), or `memory_type` skill / plan, is also written as a typed record with the raw turn as its parent (tag `routed`, idempotent on resume); unkeyed turns stay raw. Counters on `engine._role_metrics`. Taps `write.role.*`, `write.echo.*`, `write.route.*`. `false` (default): unchanged.
keys.effect: `true`: raw storage keeps every role, and derivation reads only what the role allows.

keys.description: W2-02 (LIB-29; W-04, W-05, W-08, M-08). `true`: every raw turn written by `ingest_messages` / `write_episode` is stamped. Three clocks: `source_at` from the turn's own `timestamp` (never "now"; an undated turn stays undated), `source_tz` from the turn's `tz` / `timezone` key, else `unknown`, `recorded_at` the engine clock. A naive time with no zone is kept as wall clock and recorded as `source_tz = unknown` (flagged `tz_unknown`; it is not shifted by `read.naive_timezone`); a future-skewed or out-of-order time is flagged and kept. Speaker, addressee and a `participants` list become typed columns (`spk`, `addr`, `participants`; participants are filled from the call's speakers, a turn without a name counts as its role, on by default). The provenance class comes from the role (`user_stated`, `assistant_proposed`, `tool`, `document`, `external`). A user turn that answers an assistant turn of the same call goes through the assent check: a real yes ("yes please", "sí, adelante", "ja, genau") is tagged `assent_of:<assistant record id>` for the derivation step to promote the proposal to `user_confirmed`; "ok, thanks", a refusal, a question or a conditional yes is not. Runs through the canonical intake gateway. The event interval and its precision are filled at derivation, not here. New columns `source_tz`, `participants` (Alembic `w202_stamping`). Taps `write.stamp.turn`, `write.stamp.assent`. `false` (default): turns are stamped as before.
keys.effect: `true`: every raw turn written by `ingest_messages` / `write_episode` is stamped.

On: each attachment's identity (source turn, original URI, source caption, availability) goes to the asset registry and the record is tagged `asset:<id>`. Nothing is downloaded at ingest. keys.description: O4-11 (LIB-44, O-25). `true`: `Engine.feedback` takes explicit feedback only. The `channel` (default `api`) must be `user_message`, `ui_control`, `operator_edit` or `api`; silence, dwell, regeneration, retry, copy, click, abandonment and classifier signals are refused. The actor must be the memory owner (`user` or the namespace) or a name in `write.feedback_operators` (never for a confirmation); an agent (`assistant`, `agent`, `system`, `tool`) never may. A correction, rejection or confirmation never edits a record: it becomes a bound assertion (the owner's new value, a negation of the recalled one, a restatement) written through the write door and the conflict ladder; the first written record is returned. Adds `Engine.correction_latency` (reads between a wrong memory first being surfaced and its correction, from the log; needs `event_log.mode` other than `ephemeral`). Taps: `api.feedback` (kind, channel, accepted, reason, assertions), `api.feedback.latency`. `false`: the like / dislike / note verb as before, and the new keywords are refused.

keys.description: ADR-081 optional slot for non-structured payloads (attachments, assets, large payloads, ingest blobs) by namespace and SHA-256 content hash; the event log keeps references. `null` = off. Provider `filesystem` (host-local, single-writer): `settings.root` (default `<records path>.documents`, under `deployment.data_dir` for a non-file records store), `settings.max_bytes` (default 64 MiB, refused above, never truncated), `settings.fsync` (default `true`; writes are atomic). Provider `s3` (`[aws]`, cluster, any S3-compatible store): `settings.bucket` (required), `prefix` (default `memspine/`), `endpoint_url_env` (the NAME of the variable holding a MinIO/Ceph/R2 endpoint; unset = AWS), `region`, credentials as variable names `access_key_id_env` + `secret_access_key_env` (+ `session_token_env`) or the boto3 chain (`profile`), `addressing_style`, `checksum_mode` (`when_required` for stores that reject CRC checksums), `connect_timeout_s` / `request_timeout_s` (required), `max_bytes` (default 64 MiB), `part_size_bytes` (multipart part, default 8 MiB, at least 5 MiB), `conditional_writes` (default `true`: head merges use `If-Match`), `create_bucket` (default `false`). Provider `weaviate` (`[weaviate]`, cluster, needs `deployment.id`): the vector/lexical connection settings (the same deployment shares one client) plus `max_bytes` (at most 64 MiB) and `chunk_bytes` (BLOB chunk objects, default 1 MiB, at most 4 MiB); documents are never vectorized. Provider `mongodb` (`[mongodb]`, RM-112; cluster, any process may write): a GridFS bucket `settings.bucket` (default `documents`) plus `<bucket>.heads`; `settings.url` / `database` / timeouts default to the `storage.records` MongoDB settings, so both slots on one deployment share one client (`settings.url` is required when the records store is not MongoDB); `settings.max_bytes` as above. `settings.launch` (ADR-083) unset inherits the records slot's launcher; its own `launch.mode: managed` (the `storage.records.provider` row lists the keys) runs a host-local server, one per (binary, port, data_dir) shared with a managed records slot on the same port. A started Engine exposes the store as `engine.documents` (`put`/`get`/`stream`/`head`/`delete`/`list`); a hard forget or erasure removes documents whose last referencing record (`record_ids`) was erased, and `erase_namespace` removes every document of the namespace. Removing a file is a logical delete, not physical-erasure proof.
keys.effect: Optional slot for non-structured payloads (attachments, assets, large payloads, ingest blobs) by namespace and SHA-256 content hash; the event log keeps references.

keys.description: ADR-082 (I28; was `read.decider*`): who answers the read path's yes/no decisions. `null` = the heuristic regexes and rules, unchanged and with no model. A slot `{provider, tasks, min_confidence, workers, settings}`: `provider: opendecider` runs OpenDecider-nano (`manjunathshiva/opendecider-nano`, Apache-2.0, ~400M parameters, one forward pass, a calibrated probability, no text generated) through memspine's own inference code (the `opendecider` package is not needed; install the `[decider]` extra). `tasks` (default `[list_mode, bridge_hop]`): `list_mode` replaces the set-question regex (only when `read.list_mode` is on); `needs_more_evidence` is the `decider` trigger of `read.agentic`; `bridge_hop` replaces `read.bridge_hop_gate` (only when `read.bridge_hop` is on); `about_target`. `min_confidence` (0.5..1, default 0.5): a decision below it, or any failure (dependencies or weights missing), keeps the heuristic answer. `workers` (default 1): concurrent decision calls in a bounded thread pool. OpenDecider `settings` are strict: `model` (Hugging Face id or local folder, loaded lazily once per process and device; 0.8 GB download, about 2 GB RAM in fp32), `device` (`cpu` default, `cuda`, `mps`, `auto`; one decision is about 0.2-0.4 s on a CPU), `threads` (0 = the physical cores; with `workers` > 1 each worker gets `cores // workers`), `backend` (`torch` fp32 as evaluated, or `onnx`: the published 8-bit build, CPU only, needs `onnxruntime`), `dtype` (`float32` or `bfloat16`: 300 of 300 decisions identical). Every decision is recorded in `search_forensics` under `decisions`. `Engine.set_decider(obj)` injects any object with `async decide(task, question, context) -> Decision`. `read.sensitivity_gate: decider` needs this slot.
